prerequisites: No prerequisites. Competencies taught in the Algorithms and Data Structures and Database Systems modules are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: The students can name challenges in building distributed systems.
can explain reactive, distributed programming (Actor Programming).
can explain techniques for digital representation and serialization of data (Encoding).
can describe procedures for the functioning of networks (Communication).
can specify standards for structuring and querying data (Data Models and Query Languages).
can explain algorithms and data structures for distributed data processing (Storage and Retrieval).
can describe techniques for ensuring fault tolerance and availability (Replication and Partitioning).
can describe techniques for ensuring consistency and consensus (Consistency and Consensus).
can understand algorithms for distributed transaction management (Transactions).
can explain frameworks for distributed batch processing of data-intensive tasks (Batch Processing) and for distributed data stream processing (Stream Processing).
can explain the functioning of distributed database management systems (Distributed DBMSs).
can explain the fundamentals of distributed query processing (Distributed Query Optimization).
are able to apply this knowledge practically in programming data-intensive, distributed algorithms.
are able to apply scientific working methods in independently recognizing, formulating, and solving problems.
are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Actor-, Service-, Batch- and Stream-based distributed programming
Data structures for distributed data storage

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions to at least two exercise tasks
Oral exam (individual examination) or written exam

assessment_rules: To acquire the credits, at least 50% of the points from the weekly exercise tasks must be achieved, and the solution of at least two exercise tasks must be presented orally. The examination performance is an oral or written exam. Grading is on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science program.
